subject.title: fix(streaming): preserve paragraph separators across block-streamed deliveries [AI-assisted]

question: Should the permanent block-streaming contract preserve paragraph boundaries as in-band text on chunks, carry explicit boundary metadata through delivery, or accept a narrower text-only repair for common cases?
rationale: The bug and common-case repair are clear, but the remaining maxChars boundary affects delivery limits, coalesced seams, and downstream visible reconstruction, so the durable payload contract needs maintainer direction.

options.title: Require an in-budget complete fix
options.body: Choose one candidate or replacement and require it to preserve paragraph separators at near-maxChars boundaries without over-limit chunks or doubled seams.

options.title: Move to explicit seam metadata
options.body: Ask contributors to carry paragraph/newline/hard-split metadata through chunking and delivery if text-only chunks cannot satisfy all invariants.

options.title: Accept a partial common-case repair
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally land the common-case text-only improvement while leaving the near-limit boundary documented on the canonical issue.

recommendation.title: Require an in-budget complete fix
recommendation.body: Choose one candidate or replacement and require it to preserve paragraph separators at near-maxChars boundaries without over-limit chunks or doubled seams.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has strong recent history around the coalescer, block-streaming configuration, and chunker hardening, making it the best available owner for the contract choice.
